children: Hong Kong's retail sales jumped 4.5% in value in July from a year earlier to HK$31 billion ($3.96 billion), the 15th month of gains, government data showed on Monday.
• In June, retail sales rose 4.6% on the year.
• In volume terms, July retail sales surged 2.3% from a year earlier, compared with a 2.3% rise in June.
• Stronger online retail sales growth suggests that consumer spending continued to shift toward digital channels.
• For the first seven months of 2026, the total retail sales value increased by 8.9% from a year earlier, while retail sales volume rose 6.6%.

• "Continued economic expansion, rising household incomes, and stable labour market conditions should bolster consumer sentiment," a government spokesperson said, adding upcoming events are expected to sustain growth in visitor arrivals, providing further support to retail businesses.
• The Hong Kong Tourism Board lists a fashion festival, several exhibitions and a cyclothon as upcoming events.
• However, external headwinds are still evolving and the government will monitor the impact on local consumption.
• Visitor arrivals in July rose 2.6% y/y to 4.5 million, data from the Hong Kong Tourism Board showed. The number of mainland Chinese visitors increased 2.8% y/y to 3.61 million.
• Sales of jewellery, watches, clocks and valuable gifts jumped 19.7% y/y in July after growth of 20.1% in June.
• Sales of motor vehicles and parts decreased 18.2% y/y in July following a 4.3% drop in June.
• Sales of clothing, footwear and allied products decreased 1.6% y/y in July after a 0.5% gain in June.
